hook.line: The most useful half of this sentence is the second one. You first deny a charge nobody made, then you say what you really think. It lets you criticise without picking a fight.
hook.es: No digo que esté mal, pero yo no lo haría.
hook.en: I'm not saying it's wrong, but I wouldn't do it.

examples.es: No digo que esté mal, pero yo no lo haría.
examples.en: I'm not saying it's wrong, but I wouldn't do it.

rule:
Say *No digo que* + subjunctive, then *pero* and your real point.

The verb right after *que* is always subjunctive (*esté*, *sea*, *mienta*, *tengas*), because you are refusing to claim it. The *pero* half is ordinary: *yo no lo haría*.

To sound a little injured, start with *No, si yo no digo que…*: "I never said that, but…".

Change the person on *decir*: *digo, dices, dice, decimos*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a veiled negation: you push away an accusation that nobody has made.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No digo que ___ mal, pero yo no lo haría.* (*esté* or *está*) I'm not saying it's wrong, but I wouldn't do it.
yourTurn.answer: No digo que esté mal, pero yo no lo haría.
yourTurn.why: After *no digo que* the verb takes the subjunctive, *esté*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No, si yo no digo que ___ fácil, pero se puede.* (*sea* or *es*) No, I'm not saying it's easy, but it can be done.
yourTurn.answer: No, si yo no digo que sea fácil, pero se puede.
yourTurn.why: The subjunctive *sea* keeps you from claiming it is easy.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I'm not saying Altamira is lying, but I wouldn't sign.
yourTurn.answer: No digo que Altamira mienta, pero yo no firmaría.
yourTurn.why: *Mienta* is the subjunctive, and the *pero* half is ordinary.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: We aren't saying the senator is guilty, but there are many questions.
yourTurn.answer: No decimos que el senador sea culpable, pero hay muchas preguntas.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend (informal): I'm not saying you're right, but I'm listening.
yourTurn.answer: No digo que tengas razón, pero te escucho.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *her*: *No digo que esté mal, pero yo no lo haría.* She isn't saying it's wrong, but she wouldn't do it.
yourTurn.answer: Ella no dice que esté mal, pero no lo haría.
accept: Ella no dice que esté mal, pero ella no lo haría.
yourTurn.why: *Dice* is the *she* form, and *esté* stays subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it the injured version: *No digo que sea mala, pero es muy larga.* Start with *No, si yo…*
yourTurn.answer: No, si yo no digo que sea mala, pero es muy larga.
yourTurn.why: *No, si yo no digo que…* is the veiled denial: "I never said that".

pitfalls.wrong: No digo que está mal, pero yo no lo haría.
pitfalls.right: No digo que esté mal, pero yo no lo haría.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "I'm not saying it is", but Spanish needs the subjunctive after *no digo que*.

pitfalls.wrong: No digo que esté mal, pero yo no lo haga.
pitfalls.right: No digo que esté mal, pero yo no lo haría.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Only the half after *que* is subjunctive; the *pero* half is your real statement.

pitfalls.wrong: Yo digo que no sea mala, pero es muy larga.
pitfalls.right: Yo no digo que sea mala, pero es muy larga.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The *no* goes before *digo*: you are refusing to say it, not saying the opposite.

personal: Think of a plan or a proposal at work that you have doubts about. Say your doubt with *No digo que…, pero…* so that nobody can say you were against it.
